payload.claim: Acceptance criterion 1 requires the emitted PhaseStart to carry phase `PACKAGE` and the spec's id, but every new test (`test_reverify_says_each_suites_line_through_emit_or_print`, `test_package_hands_its_emit_to_reverify`, `test_package_with_no_emit_logs_and_prints_each_re_verify_line_once`) only compares `describe(e)`, which per `saffron/events.py:921` renders `f"{event.label}: {event.detail}"` and never reads `.phase` or `.spec_id`. Changing `phase="PACKAGE"` to `phase="REVIEW"` at `saffron/phases/package.py:609` (still a valid `Phase` literal, so `types` stays green) leaves every one of these tests passing. This exact pitfall is already documented two hundred lines away in the same file: `tests/test_package.py:1587-1591` adds `assert packaged[0].phase == "PACKAGE"` specifically because `describe` ignores `phase`, citing a measured case where 1163 tests stayed green with the wrong phase. The re-verify tests added here do not repeat that guard for either `phase` or `spec_id`.
